You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 51b75b5b563a2637f9d8dc5bd02a31b2ff9e5ea0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2019 20:46:50 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] x86/mm: Check for pfn instead of page in vmalloc_sync_one()

Do not require a struct page for the mapped memory location because it
might not exist. This can happen when an ioremapped region is mapped with
2MB pages.

Fixes: 5d72b4fba40ef ('x86, mm: support huge I/O mapping capability I/F')
Signed-off-by: Joerg Roedel <jroedel@suse.de>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Reviewed-by: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20190719184652.11391-2-joro@8bytes.org

diff --git a/arch/x86/mm/fault.c b/arch/x86/mm/fault.c
index 6c46095cd0d9..e64173db4970 100644
--- a/arch/x86/mm/fault.c
+++ b/arch/x86/mm/fault.c
@@ -183,7 +183,7 @@ static inline pmd_t *vmalloc_sync_one(pgd_t *pgd, unsigned long address)
 	if (!pmd_present(*pmd))
 		set_pmd(pmd, *pmd_k);
 	else
-		BUG_ON(pmd_page(*pmd) != pmd_page(*pmd_k));
+		BUG_ON(pmd_pfn(*pmd) != pmd_pfn(*pmd_k));
 
 	return pmd_k;
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/mm/fault.c`**
   - The line that checks if the page mapped by `pmd` is the same as the page mapped by `pmd_k` has been modified. 
   - The original line:
     ```c
     BUG_ON(pmd_page(*pmd) != pmd_page(*pmd_k));
     ```
   - Has been changed to:
     ```c
     BUG_ON(pmd_pfn(*pmd) != pmd_pfn(*pmd_k));
     ```
   - This change alters the check from comparing the struct page to comparing the page frame number (PFN), which allows for the handling of mapped memory locations that may not have an associated struct page, particularly in cases involving 2MB pages.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `fault.c` addresses a specific issue related to the handling of memory mappings in the x86 architecture. By changing the check from a struct page comparison to a PFN comparison, the patch resolves a potential bug that could occur when dealing with ioremap regions mapped with larger page sizes (2MB). This change is directly linked to the bug fix mentioned in the patch description, ensuring that the system can correctly handle scenarios where a struct page may not exist for certain memory mappings.

        Rank these code statements based on their relevance to the root cause of the bug.
        
        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the assumption that a struct page is always available for a mapped memory location. This assumption fails in cases where an ioremapped region is mapped using 2MB pages, leading to potential incorrect behavior when checking the mapped memory. The original code compares struct pages, which may not exist, instead of using the page frame number (PFN) that can correctly identify the mapping regardless of the presence of a struct page.
